cands.bio: Democrat representing California's 13th District in the U.S. House since January 2025. Served in the California State Assembly from 2012 to 2022. Earlier worked as a staffer for several state legislators. Teaches a course on the California Legislature at UC Merced and helps lead a small business.

controversies.text: Federal records show $5,000 from AIPAC's PAC since 2021; $41,704 from individuals passed through that PAC in 2025-26.
Missed 40 of 676 U.S. House votes this Congress (5.9%), counted from the roll calls through 2026-09-16. Longest run of misses: 15, 2025-09-15 to 2025-09-18.

The Los Angeles Times reported in August 2024 that a company in which Gray holds a minority stake bought Castle Air Force Base apartments in 2022. The state gave the site nearly $50 million the next year. Experts said no law appeared broken. Gray's campaign called the allegations false and said he has made no profit.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, the California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), the California Teachers Association, and IUOE Local 3.
The California Fraternal Order of Police endorsed his 2026 re-election, per his campaign press release listing (Sep 15, 2026).
The Modesto Police Officers' Association endorsed his 2026 re-election, per his campaign press release listing (Jul 30, 2026).

cands.gaps: We found no stated positions or actions from Gray on data centers, homestead property tax relief, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, guns, abortion, or school vouchers and charters. We found no documented stance of his on development or growth limits. Part of his campaign site's issues page was cut off, so some of what he says there could not be read. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey, so his own answers on these topics are not on record there. The campaign-site claims about his Assembly-era positions, such as opposing Props 25, 47 and 57, come from his own site and were not checked against legislative records.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

cands.bio: Republican and U.S. Marine Corps veteran. Served on Marine One, then worked as a district manager at a private security company and as executive pastor of a Stockton church. Mayor of Stockton from 2021 to 2024. Lost the 2024 race for CA-9 and ran in CA-13 in 2026.

endorsements.text: Endorsed by Donald Trump for the 2026 race, per Ballotpedia's endorsement list.
Endorsed by the Republican Party of California, per Ballotpedia.
Endorsed by the San Joaquin County Republican Party, per Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: We found no records of specific decisions Lincoln made as mayor or as a city leader on housing, development, data centers, property taxes, or land and water. We found no documented statements from him on homestead property taxes, foreign or investor ownership of homes and land, firearms laws, abortion, or H-1B visas. His claims about police pay and the budget come only from his own campaign site. We found no news reporting on controversies and no information on foreign ties. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. The sources we had disagree on whether his term as mayor ended in 2024 or 2025.

qual.background: Mayor of Stockton (2021 to 2024), a city executive and elected office. Earlier a district manager at a private security company, with a reported $55 million budget and more than 1,300 employees. Marine Corps veteran and church executive pastor.
qual.why: He has held local elected executive office and managed a large budget and workforce, which fits the middle range. He has no legislative or legal background and has not held a federal or state office.

stop-data-centers.evidence: His campaign site says he supports the President's AI Action Plan, which it says removes burdensome regulations and builds out domestic AI infrastructure.

workers-first.evidence: His campaign site says he will fight to secure the border, enforce immigration laws and restore law and order.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says that as mayor he backed police with an 18% pay raise and a $42 million budget increase. It also says he will fight soft-on-crime policies such as early prisoner release. These are the campaign's own claims, and no other page confirms them.
